title: New stars shed light on the past
caption: The star-forming region N90 in the Small Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: N90, NGC 602 · constellation Hydrus · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration

recognition.text: Ranked #16 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Bright blue stars, freshly formed, sit inside a hollow they have carved in the middle of a nebula. Around them, the cloud's outer reaches remain, and beyond those a scattering of distant galaxies shows through, tinted reddish-brown by dust. This is N90, a star-forming region in the Small Magellanic Cloud, a small companion galaxy of the Milky Way.

The young stars are hot, and they pour out high-energy radiation. That radiation is wearing the nebula away from the inside. The thin outer parts of the cloud stop the energetic outflows from escaping straight out of the cluster, so the erosion works on the nebula's edges from within.

N90 sits well away from the main body of the Small Magellanic Cloud. Because of that position, many far more distant galaxies can be seen in Hubble's view. They sit far behind the young stars, and dust in the region gives them a reddish-brown tint.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.13 x 3.05 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 182 × 177 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded this scene through visible, near-infrared and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared filter captures light the eye cannot see, and Hubble's long exposures reveal faint background galaxies far beyond what any eye could detect.

explore: The region, also cataloged with the star cluster NGC 602, is listed at a distance of about 200,000 light-years, in the direction of the constellation Hydrus. The image comes from the Hubble Heritage Team working with the ESA/Hubble collaboration.
alt: Bright blue young stars inside a cavity in a nebula, with many small reddish-brown background galaxies visible around it.
